analysis:
The changed file is fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json, a golden-vector test fixture for the prompt contract. The supplied units are two BASE-side text excerpts (lines 39601-41614) covering gpt-oss-20b and qwen3.5-35b-a3b cases. These contain token IDs, request/provider bodies and template inputs. They are test data, not executable code, authorization logic, key handling, attestation or transport. The patch excerpt is truncated but shows a qwen case gaining an `additional_context: {enable_thinking: false}` member in template_input, a reduced prompt_token_count (803 to 767), changed block_boundaries and chain_hash values, and token ID changes. The hunk coordinates imply other base/head changes at 43813-54138, which are not visible in the supplied units.

I found no concrete security regression in the visible evidence. Fixture changes alone do not touch the TB-002/TB-011 gates (encrypted transport, App Attest authorization, final handoff). Prompt-contract IDs, chain hashes and block boundaries are cache-routing and prefix-cache identity inputs relevant to T-041. The visible evidence does not show a change to cache-isolation scope or to scope_id handling, and it does not show any key, scope or plaintext exposure.

Residual questions for later passes, none of which are findings:
- Whether the production code that consumes these vectors (the prompt contract and template renderer) was changed consistently. Examples would be the `additional_context` injection and the shortened prompt token count, including whether the new cache chain hashes are still scoped per tenant.
- Whether `enable_thinking: false` injected from provider or coordinator code can be influenced by a consumer to change cache keys across tenants.

The head side and the remaining patch hunks were not supplied, so the cache-key semantics are unverified. The base-text excerpts also contain only the pre-change state.
